join-all.title: How futures::future::join_all works
join-all.description: Runs many futures concurrently and collects all their outputs, in order.

slides.caption: All futures make progress together; join_all finishes when the last one does.
Their outputs come back as a Vec, in input order.
Concurrent, not parallel: spawn tasks if you need several threads.

try-join-all.title: How futures::future::try_join_all works
try-join-all.description: Like join_all for Result futures: stops at the first error.

slides.caption: If every future succeeds you get Ok(vec). The first error ends it, and the other futures are dropped.

join.title: How futures::future::join works
join.description: Waits for two futures concurrently and returns both outputs.

slides.caption: The outputs may have different types. join3..join5 for more.
The join! macro takes any number of futures.

try-join.title: How futures::future::try_join works
try-join.description: Waits for two Result futures; the first error wins.

slides.caption: An Err from either ends it early.

select.title: How futures::future::select works
select.description: Waits for whichever of two futures finishes first.

slides.caption: The result tells you which side won, and gives you the other, unfinished future back.
The left future is ready first.
Left with its value and the still-pending right future.
Both futures must be Unpin: pin them with Box::pin or pin! first.

select-all.title: How futures::future::select_all works
select-all.description: Waits for the first of many futures; returns its output, its index and the rest.

slides.caption: The remaining futures can be awaited again.

ready.title: How futures::future::ready works
ready.description: A future that is immediately ready with a value.

slides.caption: Useful when an API needs a future but you already have the value.
Handy as a placeholder branch in select.
now_or_never shows it is not ready.

lazy.title: How futures::future::lazy works
lazy.description: A future that runs a closure the first time it is polled.

slides.caption: Creating it does nothing; awaiting it runs the closure.
async { } blocks behave the same way.

poll-fn.title: How futures::future::poll_fn works
poll-fn.description: Makes a future from a closure that is called on every poll.

slides.caption: Return Poll::Pending (and arrange a wake-up) to wait.
std::future::poll_fn is the same since Rust 1.64.

future-map.title: How FutureExt::map works
future-map.description: Transforms a future's output when it completes.

slides.caption: The closure is sync; use then for async.

future-then.title: How FutureExt::then works
future-then.description: Chains another future that depends on the first output.

slides.caption: Inside async code, just use .await twice.

future-boxed.title: How FutureExt::boxed works
future-boxed.description: Puts a future in a Pin<Box<dyn Future + Send>>.

slides.caption: Needed to store different futures in one Vec or to return them from trait methods.

now-or-never.title: How FutureExt::now_or_never works
now-or-never.description: Polls a future once: Some(output) if it is already done, else None.

slides.caption: Mostly for tests and sync glue.

future-fuse.title: How FutureExt::fuse works
future-fuse.description: Makes a future safe to poll again after it has finished (it then stays pending).

future-shared.title: How FutureExt::shared works
future-shared.description: Lets several places await the same future and all get (a clone of) its output.

slides.caption: The output must be Clone; the work runs once.

map-ok.title: How TryFutureExt::map_ok works
map-ok.description: Maps the Ok value of a Result future.

and-then.title: How TryFutureExt::and_then works
and-then.description: Chains another fallible future after a success.

slides.caption: Skipped when the first future fails.

map-err-fut.title: How TryFutureExt::map_err works
map-err-fut.description: Maps the error of a Result future.

stream-iter.title: How futures::stream::iter works
stream-iter.description: Turns an iterator into a stream that is always ready.

slides.caption: A Stream is the async version of Iterator: you await each next item.
The first next().await yields 1 at once.
Use it to feed stream combinators with known data.

stream-once.title: How futures::stream::once works
stream-once.description: A stream with exactly one item, produced by a future.

stream-repeat.title: How futures::stream::repeat works
stream-repeat.description: An endless stream of clones of one value.

slides.caption: Always limit it with take or zip.
repeat_with calls a closure each time.

stream-unfold.title: How futures::stream::unfold works
stream-unfold.description: Builds a stream from a state and an async step function.

slides.caption: Each step returns the next item and the new state; None ends the stream.
Great for paginated APIs: the state is the page token.

stream-select.title: How futures::stream::select works
stream-select.description: Merges two streams, taking items from whichever is ready (alternating when both are).

stream-next.title: How StreamExt::next works
stream-next.description: Awaits the next item of a stream: Some(item), or None at the end.

slides.caption: next() is to streams what Iterator::next is to iterators, with an .await.
The stream must be Unpin; pin it with pin! or Box::pin otherwise.

stream-map.title: How StreamExt::map works
stream-map.description: Transforms each item with a sync closure.

slides.caption: For async work per item use then.

stream-filter.title: How StreamExt::filter works
stream-filter.description: Keeps the items for which an async predicate returns true.

slides.caption: The predicate returns a future (often future::ready).
filter_map filters and maps at once.

stream-filter-map.title: How StreamExt::filter_map works
stream-filter-map.description: Maps each item to an Option asynchronously; keeps the Somes.

stream-then.title: How StreamExt::then works
stream-then.description: Runs an async closure for each item, one at a time.

slides.caption: Sequential: the next item starts after the previous finishes.

stream-collect.title: How StreamExt::collect works
stream-collect.description: Gathers every item into a collection.

stream-fold.title: How StreamExt::fold works
stream-fold.description: Reduces a stream to one value with an async closure.

title.text: s.fold(0, |acc, x| async move { acc + x })

stream-for-each.title: How StreamExt::for_each works
stream-for-each.description: Runs an async closure for every item, in order.

slides.caption: A while let loop is the explicit form.

stream-for-each-concurrent.title: How StreamExt::for_each_concurrent works
stream-for-each-concurrent.description: Runs the closure for up to n items at the same time.

slides.caption: None as the limit means no limit.
Start the next as one finishes.
Order of completion is not guaranteed.

stream-take.title: How StreamExt::take works
stream-take.description: Ends the stream after n items.

slides.caption: The skipped items are still produced, then thrown away.

stream-take-while.title: How StreamExt::take_while works
stream-take-while.description: Yields items while an async predicate holds, then ends.

slides.caption: Ends at the first failing item; later items are not checked.

stream-chain.title: How StreamExt::chain works
stream-chain.description: Yields one stream's items, then another's.

slides.caption: The second starts after the first ends.

stream-zip.title: How StreamExt::zip works
stream-zip.description: Pairs items of two streams; ends when either ends.

slides.caption: Waits for an item from both sides each time.

stream-enumerate.title: How StreamExt::enumerate works
stream-enumerate.description: Pairs each item with its index.

stream-flat-map.title: How StreamExt::flat_map works
stream-flat-map.description: Maps each item to a stream and flattens them in order.

slides.caption: Each inner stream is drained before the next starts.
flatten() when items already are streams.

stream-buffered.title: How StreamExt::buffered works
stream-buffered.description: Runs up to n of the stream's futures at once, yielding results in the original order.

slides.caption: Each item is a future. Up to n of them run concurrently; outputs are still delivered in order.
Results come out in order; fut 3 starts when a slot frees.
buffer_unordered yields in completion order instead.

stream-buffer-unordered.title: How StreamExt::buffer_unordered works
stream-buffer-unordered.description: Runs up to n futures at once, yielding each result as soon as it is ready.

slides.caption: The usual way to limit concurrency for many requests.

stream-chunks.title: How StreamExt::chunks works
stream-chunks.description: Groups items into Vecs of up to n.

slides.caption: The last batch may be smaller.

stream-count.title: How StreamExt::count works
stream-count.description: Counts the items of a stream.

stream-any.title: How StreamExt::any works
stream-any.description: true if any item satisfies an async predicate.

stream-peekable.title: How StreamExt::peekable works
stream-peekable.description: A stream whose next item you can look at without taking it.

slides.caption: peek needs a pinned stream: pin!(s) or Box::pin.

try-collect.title: How TryStreamExt::try_collect works
try-collect.description: Collects the Ok items; stops at the first Err.

slides.caption: With an Err anywhere, that Err is returned.

try-next.title: How TryStreamExt::try_next works
try-next.description: Like next(), but returns Result<Option<T>>, so ? works in loops.

slides.caption: An Err item comes back as Err.

try-stream-map-ok.title: How TryStreamExt::map_ok works
try-stream-map-ok.description: Maps the Ok items of a stream of Results.

try-filter.title: How TryStreamExt::try_filter works
try-filter.description: Filters the Ok items with an async predicate; errors pass.

try-for-each.title: How TryStreamExt::try_for_each works
try-for-each.description: Runs a fallible async closure per item; stops at the first error.

slides.caption: Errors from the stream or the closure end it.
